short: The naturalist who explained the diversity of life through natural selection.
full:
Darwin's five-year voyage on HMS Beagle from 1831 gave him the observations — South American fossils, the geology of the Andes, the finches and mockingbirds of the Galápagos — from which he built his theory. He then spent more than twenty years accumulating evidence before publishing.

On the Origin of Species appeared in 1859 and sold out immediately. Its argument is disarmingly simple: organisms vary, variation is heritable, more are born than can survive, and so the variants best suited to their circumstances leave more offspring. Repeated over deep time, this alone accounts for adaptation and the branching relatedness of all living things. It remains the organising principle of biology.
